small_guidance:
- The fused softmax+sigmoid kernel is already memory-bound and small relative to the conv; further tuning here yields little. Try adding configs with `BLOCK_S=1024, num_warps=8` and `num_stages=3` keyed on `(C,S)`, and consider one-program-per-(N, S-tile) with `BLOCK_C=64` (exact C) so the channel dim is a single tile and the reduction stays in registers.
- Ensure the store mask uses `mask_c[:,None] & mask_s[None,:]` (currently fine) and consider writing in fp32 with vectorized `BLOCK_S` powers-of-two only.
- Bigger lever: the ConvTranspose3d dominates runtime (~8-9ms of the 10.1ms). No amount of softmax tuning will move `fast_p` past ~0.55.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per `(N, IC-tile, D_in, H_in tile, W_in tile)` computing the input×kernel outer product and atomically (or via deterministic accumulation per output tile) scattering into the output grid, handling stride=2, padding=1, output_padding=1 in index math. Fuse bias-add into the same epilogue.
- Alternatively, formulate ConvTranspose3d as a gather-style GEMM: one program per `(N, OC-tile, output-spatial-tile)`, where each output position gathers the contributing `(ic, kd, kh, kw)` taps (only those satisfying `(od+pad-kd) % stride == 0` and in-range), accumulating into a tile. Use `channels_last_3d` layout so IC is the contiguous GEMM-K axis. Start with safe tiles `(BM,BN,BK)=(32,32,16)` num_warps=4 num_stages=2 inside `triton.autotune`.
- Fuse the channel-softmax+sigmoid into the conv-transpose epilogue when feasible: have the conv kernel produce a full OC vector per spatial point in registers/SMEM, then do the max/sum/exp/sigmoid before storing — eliminates a full read/write pass over the 16×64×32×64×64 output tensor.
